# @zakkster/lite-audio
> Zero-GC reactive Web Audio engine. Signal-driven buses, ABA-safe voice handles, unlock queue, per-bus AudioPool, streaming music tracks with equal-power crossfade.

## Install
npm i @zakkster/lite-audio @zakkster/lite-signal @zakkster/lite-audio-pool

## Import
import { LiteAudio, VERSION } from '@zakkster/lite-audio';
// VERSION is the package version string, in lockstep with package.json.

## Key Facts
- Zero deps of its own; two peers: @zakkster/lite-signal (^1.3), @zakkster/lite-audio-pool (^1.2)
- Signal-driven control surface: bus volumes, master mute, ctx state, per-sound and per-track load state are all reactive
- Bus writes go through setTargetAtTime for click-free transitions (10 ms time constant)
- Pre-unlock play() calls are queued (bounded, latest-per-sound), flushed on first user gesture
- iOS/Safari unlock: silent-buffer pulse + resume() on touchstart/touchend/mousedown/keydown (capture phase, exact set the manager uses)
- Handles 'interrupted' state (iOS phone-call scenario) the same as 'suspended'
- Master mute persists to localStorage under 'lite_audio_muted' (byte-identical to lite-audio-manager for migration)
- One AudioPool per bus for SFX (pool v1.1.0+ output param + per-play buffer override)
- Music tracks stream via MediaElementAudioSourceNode routed through the same bus graph
- Positional hot path for SFX: play(soundId, volume, pan, pitch) - no options object per call
- SFX handles are bus-tagged: busIndex * 2^32 + poolHandle. Raw pool handles collide across buses (every pool starts at channel 0 / generation 0), so the tag is what makes stop() name one voice
- Music tracks are singletons addressed by name, not handle - stopTrack('menu_bg') not stop(handle)
- v2.0.0 ships SFX + music + mix intelligence (ducking, snapshots, auto-suspend, per-bus meters, dynamic buses) + a `./compat` drop-in for lite-audio-manager (the Howler overlay). Migrate by changing one import; no Howler underneath.
- v2.1.0 adds positional audio: createBus(name,{spatial:'positional'}) builds a PannerNode per voice and setPosition(handle,x,y,z) writes 3D position on the cold ~10 Hz monitor (zero-alloc scratch stamp on the caller frame, fail-closed on a stolen handle). Default stays 'stereo', byte-identical; the hot play() gains no new branch.
- v2.2.0 adds an HRTF spatial bus: createBus(name,{spatial:'hrtf'}) is positional-family (same distance graph + setPosition()) but the pool sets the PannerNode's panningModel='HRTF' for per-voice binaural convolution. Headphones-only (a stereo speaker setup hears no benefit and pays the CPU), and each live HRTF voice costs a per-voice HRTF convolution -- budget it. A silent gain=0 HRIR prewarm voice fires post-unlock and retires on the next monitor tick so the browser loads the impulse-response set up front and the FIRST real play does not stutter. lite-audio never sets panningModel itself (the pool owns its spatial nodes); the hot play()/setPosition() paths gain zero new branches (the 'positional'||'hrtf' OR collapses once at cold bus construction into a derived flag). Requires @zakkster/lite-audio-pool ^1.4.0.
- v2.3.0 adds a per-bus stereo widener: createBus(name,{width:0..1}) inserts a mono-safe Haas widener between the pool output and bus.gain -- the dry (mono) signal plus a delayed/opposite-panned wet pair (12 ms left, 19 ms right, hard-panned -1/+1) summed back through an explicit makeup gain (1/sqrt(1+4*wet^2)) so opening width holds total power flat (0 dB, SP-05). setWidth(busName,w) is a caller-frame method that rides the cold ~10 Hz monitor: it only clamps to [0,1] and stamps a target + dirty bit (zero alloc, no per-frame ramp), and the wet/makeup params are written at most once per tick when the value moves. width:0 is a bit-identical bypass (after a short settle the flush snaps wet to EXACTLY 0 and makeup to EXACTLY 1 with setValueAtTime, since setTargetAtTime never reaches its target). MONO-SOURCE-ONLY: a Haas widener smears a stereo asset, so a non-mono loaded buffer DISARMS the widener at pool build (widthRefused='stereo-source', setWidth becomes a no-op) and width>0 on a positional/hrtf bus is a construction-time RangeError (the stereo widener does not compose with per-voice panning). The comb-filter mono-downmix hazard (SP-04) is real -- on a single-speaker / mono playback the delayed copies sum into audible notches, so budget the widener for headphone/stereo output. No boolean API: there is deliberately no enableWidth/on toggle, only the width:0..1 knob (0 == off). widthOf(busName) reads the current width or null on an unarmed/disarmed/unknown bus. Default (no width option) is byte-identical to prior releases: no widener nodes, the hot play()/stop() paths gain zero new branches.
- v2.4.0 adds fail-closed output-layout detection and a 7+1 discrete-surround bus. _detectLayout() runs ONCE at init() and reads destination.maxChannelCount; it accepts ONLY a concrete integer >= 8 (Number.isInteger(v) && v >= 8) -> layoutOf()==='7.1', everything else (absent, undefined, null, NaN, non-integer, string, or < 8) -> 'stereo'. createBus(name,{spatial:'discrete',preset:'7.1'}) rides the pool's discrete mode with 8 SMPTE lanes (0=L 1=R 2=C 3=LFE 4=SL 5=SR 6=SBL 7=SBR) and per-voice VBAP panning via the SAME setPosition(handle,x,y,z) -- but ONLY when layoutOf()==='7.1'; on a smaller sink the discrete request transparently falls back to a WORKING stereo bus (lanes=0) and effectiveLayoutOf(name) reports 'stereo' so the caller can see it -- that fallback is correct, not a failure. The 8-lane solve rides the cold ~10 Hz monitor (_flushLanes): az=atan2(x,-z) picks a constant-power (VBAP) speaker pair on a 7-lane ring (g1=cos(f*PI/2), g2=sin(f*PI/2)); the LFE lane (index 3) gets an azimuth-invariant distance-only send, never a VBAP gain; y (height) is not panned. All 8 lane gains written with setTargetAtTime at the same 20 ms/~10 Hz cadence as position, into one reused module Float32Array(8) -- zero alloc, rate-bounded. destination.channelCount is mutated to 8/explicit/discrete ONLY on the first discrete pool build (process-global for the context) and restored on destroy(). preset '5.1'/'3.1' reject loudly (a later release); width>0 or hrtf never composes with discrete (RangeError). Requires @zakkster/lite-audio-pool ^1.4.0.
- v2.5.0 adds the 5+1 (6-lane) and 3+1 (4-lane) reductions of the discrete-surround bus plus a cold fallback LADDER, and WIDENS layoutOf() from '7.1'|'stereo' to the richest single layout the sink carries: Number.isInteger(v) && v>=8 -> '7.1', 6|7 -> '5.1', 4|5 -> '3.1', else 'stereo' (still resolved once at init(), cached). BEHAVIOR CHANGE: a real 4/6ch sink that returned 'stereo' under 2.4.0 now returns '3.1'/'5.1'; the two S6 tokens keep their meaning (=== '7.1' only on a >=8 sink), and a 2ch sink is unchanged ('stereo'). createBus(name,{spatial:'discrete',preset:'5.1'|'3.1'}) no longer throws -- each builds the pool in the matching channels:6|4 mode; the LADDER resolves the built layout as the largest preset whose channel-need <= min(request-need, maxChannels), stepping down 7.1->5.1->3.1->stereo, and NEVER upgrades (a '5.1' request on an 8ch sink stays '5.1'). effectiveLayoutOf(name) reports the BUILT token ('7.1'/'5.1'/'3.1'/'stereo'/null). Lane indices are shared SMPTE: 5.1 ring drops SBL/SBR (lanes 0-5), 3.1 is front-only (lanes 0-3, L R C LFE); LFE stays index 3, azimuth-invariant, in every preset; 3.1 has no rear speaker (a source behind folds across the 300-degree back gap between R and L -- correct for a front-only rig). The solver is generalized to a cold, data-driven walk of a per-preset frozen ring record captured at bus construction (busRec.vbap), so _flushLanes writes EXACTLY busRec.lanes gains (8/6/4) with NO per-tick preset branch, reusing the single Float32Array(8) scratch; play()/setPosition() gain zero new branches. destination.channelCount is set to the MAX lane count across live discrete buses (monotonic, add-only), pristine triple saved once and restored on destroy(). Peer stays @zakkster/lite-audio-pool ^1.4.0 (pool has shipped channels:{4,6,8} since 1.3.0). See decisions/0009.
- Mix automation lives on a per-bus sidechain gain (gain -> duckGain -> master) so ducking and snapshot morphs compose with volume/mute instead of fighting for one AudioParam. Meters / duck follower / auto-suspend / position flush / lane flush / width flush share one cold ~10 Hz monitor that never touches play()/stop().

## Quick Start
```js
import { LiteAudio } from '@zakkster/lite-audio';

const audio = new LiteAudio();            // buses default to sfx/ui/voice/music
await audio.init();

// SFX
await audio.defineSounds({
    laser: { src: ['/laser.opus', '/laser.mp3'], bus: 'sfx' },
    click: { src: ['/click.mp3'], bus: 'ui' },
});
const h = audio.play('laser', 0.8, 0.0, 1.0);
audio.stop(h);

// Music
await audio.defineTracks({
    menu:     { src: ['/menu.mp3'], bus: 'music' },
    gameplay: { src: ['/gameplay.mp3'], bus: 'music',
                loop: true, loopStart: 4.5, loopEnd: 92 },
});
audio.playTrack('menu', { fadeIn: 400 });
audio.crossfade('menu', 'gameplay', 500);
audio.stopTrack('gameplay', { fade: 300 });

// Reactive readouts
audio.unlocked();                         // ReadSignal<boolean>
audio.trackPlaying('gameplay');           // ReadSignal<boolean>
audio.trackPosition('gameplay');          // ReadSignal<number>, throttled ~10 Hz
audio.setMuted(true);                     // master mute, persists to localStorage

audio.destroy();                          // idempotent
```

## Export: LiteAudio (class)

### Constructor
```
new LiteAudio(opts?)
```
- `opts.buses?: string[]` - defaults ['sfx', 'ui', 'voice', 'music']. 'master' is implicit.
- `opts.poolCapacity?: number` - defaults 32 (SFX per bus).
- `opts.queueLimit?: number` - defaults 32 (pre-unlock queue).
- `opts.mutedStorageKey?: string` - defaults 'lite_audio_muted'.
- `opts.fetch?, opts.window?, opts.document?` - test injectables.
- `opts.setTimeout?, opts.clearTimeout?` - test injectables for stopTrack teardown.

### async init(ctx?): Promise<void>
Wires the engine to an AudioContext. Creates one via globalThis.AudioContext if none passed. Sets up master gain, bus gains, master-mute effect, per-bus volume+mute effects, statechange listener, unlock listeners.

### SFX (v1.0.0)

async defineSounds(config): fetch + decodeAudioData every sound. Config `{ [id]: { src: string[], bus?, volume?, pitchVar? } }`.
play(soundId, volume?, pan?, pitch?): positional hot path, returns handle >= 0 or -1.
playOpts(soundId, opts?): sugar with pitchVar resolution.
stop(handle): stops a specific play. The handle carries its bus, so stop() resolves the owning pool in O(1) and can never reach across a bus boundary.
isPlaying(handle): boolean. busOf(handle): string|null. activeCount(busName?): live SFX voices per bus or engine-wide.
setPosition(handle, x, y, z): set a positional voice's 3D position. Takes the SAME handle play() returned. Caller-frame safe (call every frame): does NO param write -- it only stamps a preallocated scratch buffer + a dirty bit, zero allocation. The positionX/Y/Z writes ride the shared ~10 Hz monitor (throttled, 0.02 s time constant), so per-frame calls collapse to ~10 native param events/second per axis (the SP-03 bound). Fail-closed: a stereo-bus handle, an out-of-range channel, or a stolen/dead/bogus voice is a silent no-op (steal-safety resolves at flush via a generation-checked voiceNode, so a stolen channel never gets the stale position). Requires a bus built with {spatial:'positional'}.
stopBus(name, opts?), stopAll(opts?): bus- and engine-wide stops. Both stop SFX voices AND fade out any music track routed to those buses (opts.fade, default 200ms).
loadState(id): ReadSignal<'idle'|'loading'|'ready'|'error'>.

### Music (v1.1.0)

async defineTracks(config): fetch + attach <audio> elements for streaming. Config `{ [name]: { src: string[], bus?, volume?, loop?, loopStart?, loopEnd? } }`.
playTrack(name, opts?): starts or resumes. Opts `{ fadeIn?, position?, restart? }`. Idempotent unless restart.
stopTrack(name, { fade? }): fades out, pauses element after fade. Playing signal flips false immediately.
pauseTrack(name) / resumeTrack(name): position preserved.
crossfade(from, to, durationMs): equal-power both sides. Either side can be null.
playExclusive(name, opts?): bus-scoped - fades other playing tracks on same bus.
playUnique(name, thresholdMs = 100): timestamp gate, works on sounds AND tracks. Returns a handle for a sound, -2 for a track (singleton, name-addressed), -1 on rejection or unknown. Never 0 for a track - 0 is a real handle.
trackLoadState(name), trackPlaying(name), trackPosition(name), trackDuration(name): per-track signals.

### Crossfade semantics
- Equal-power curves precomputed at module load (128 samples each: EQ_POWER_IN, EQ_POWER_OUT). Per-call scaled Float32Array per side is the only allocation, off the hot path (scene transitions).
- Interruption (case c): only tracks named in the new call are touched. A track fading out from a previous crossfade keeps its schedule. A track being retargeted reads its current xfadeGain value and starts an equal-power ramp scaled from that value - no discontinuities.
- Graph: <audio> -> MediaElementSource -> xfadeGain (0..1 crossfade knob) -> volumeGain (baseline volume) -> bus.gain

### Bus + master
setBusVolume(name, v), setBusMuted(name, m), setMuted(state): signal setters. Every write schedules setTargetAtTime with a 10 ms time constant.

### Mix intelligence (v1.2.0)

duck(bus, level, {attack, release}): dip a bus's sidechain to `level` (0..1 multiplier under volume/mute) over the attack TC. Manual and always-wins - latches the bus out of any follower until stopDuck().
stopDuck(bus, {release}): restore to rest over the release TC, clearing the manual latch.
duckOn(triggerBus, targetBus, {threshold=1, level=0.3, attack, release}): automatic follower - while triggerBus has >= threshold voices, dip targetBus. Off the hot path, edge-only. Explicit duck() wins. Attack/release asymmetric by default.
captureSnapshot(name): record every bus's volume + mute (not track volumes).
applySnapshot(name, ms): morph to it over ms. Signals truthful immediately; audible transition rides the sidechain, continuous from the actual current level (click-free mid-morph / mid-duck). ms=0 snaps.
createBus(name, {meter, spatial}): create a bus after init(). Idempotent, rejects 'master', fails closed (RangeError) at the 2^21 ceiling at runtime. {meter:true} taps an AnalyserNode. {spatial:'positional'} builds a PannerNode per voice (default 'stereo' = StereoPanner equalpower, byte-identical to prior releases) and enables setPosition(). {spatial:'hrtf'} is positional-family (same PannerNode distance graph + setPosition()) but the pool sets panningModel='HRTF' for per-voice binaural convolution -- headphones-only, higher CPU; a silent HRIR prewarm fires post-unlock to eat the first-play hitch. {spatial:'discrete',preset:'7.1'} builds a 7+1 discrete-surround bus under a detected 7.1 sink and falls back to stereo otherwise (see "Discrete surround" below). An unknown spatial value fails closed with a did-you-mean. Spatial mode is decided here at construction and captured into the pool's panner option -- the hot play() never re-tests it.
level(bus): ReadSignal<number> RMS at ~10 Hz, or null on an unmetered/unknown bus. One pre-allocated Float32Array per metered bus, zero alloc per read.
enableAutoSuspend({after=30}): suspend the context after N silent seconds; a later play() wakes it (bare resume(), native scheduler holds the voice). Returns false and stays off on iOS (un-unlock hazard). disableAutoSuspend(), isAutoSuspended().

### Discrete surround (v2.4.0)

layoutOf(): the engine's detected output layout, '7.1' or 'stereo', resolved once at init() and cached (a mid-session device/headset change does NOT re-detect). Fail-closed: only a destination.maxChannelCount that is a concrete integer >= 8 yields '7.1'; absent / undefined / null / NaN / non-integer / string / < 8 all yield 'stereo'. null is not zero -- an unknown sink is stereo, never optimistically 7.1.
createBus(name, {spatial:'discrete', preset:'7.1'}): a 7+1 discrete-surround bus. Under a detected 7.1 sink it builds the pool in discrete mode with 8 lanes and enables setPosition() for per-voice VBAP panning; under any smaller sink it fails closed to a plain STEREO bus (lanes=0) that plays normally. preset is only valid with spatial:'discrete' (a preset elsewhere is a RangeError); S6 ships only '7.1' -- '5.1'/'3.1' reject loudly rather than silently degrade. spatial:'discrete' does not compose with a width widener (RangeError) and, being one enum field, cannot combine with 'hrtf'.
effectiveLayoutOf(name): '7.1' when the 8 lanes were actually built, 'stereo' when a discrete request fell back, null on a non-discrete or unknown bus. This is how a caller learns the fallback happened -- e.g. on a 2-channel sink a discrete request returns 'stereo' here, and that is the correct, supported outcome.
setPosition(handle, x, y, z): the SAME zero-alloc caller-frame stamp positional/hrtf buses use -- a discrete bus reuses the identical posXYZ/posOwner/posDirty scratch and gains no new branch. The 8 lane gains are solved and written on the cold ~10 Hz monitor (_flushLanes), throttled with a 20 ms setTargetAtTime, so per-frame calls collapse to ~10 native events/lane/second. Lane order is frozen SMPTE (0=L 1=R 2=C 3=LFE 4=SL 5=SR 6=SBL 7=SBR). LFE (index 3) carries only a distance-only send, never a VBAP gain. y (height) has no 7+1 lane and is deliberately not panned.
Hazards: the 8-lane render is audible only on a real >= 8ch sink; a virtual-surround headset that reports maxChannelCount 2 gets the stereo fallback (correct). Mutating destination.channelCount is process-global for the context (done once on the first discrete pool, restored on destroy); a caller mixing a discrete bus with an assumed-stereo external graph on the same context is unsupported.

### Discrete subsets (v2.5.0)

v2.5.0 widens layoutOf() and adds the 5+1 and 3+1 presets. layoutOf() now reports the RICHEST single layout the sink carries (still one-shot at init, cached):

  maxChannelCount (Number.isInteger only)   layoutOf()
  >= 8                                      '7.1'
  6 or 7                                    '5.1'
  4 or 5                                    '3.1'
  < 4 / 2 / non-integer / NaN / null / absent   'stereo'

createBus(name,{spatial:'discrete',preset:'5.1'|'3.1'|'7.1'}) resolves the BUILT layout down a cold fallback ladder -- the largest preset whose channel-need <= min(request-need, maxChannels). Channel needs: 7.1->8, 5.1->6, 3.1->4. The 12-cell requested x M ladder (M = detected max channels):

  requested / M    >= 8     6 or 7    4 or 5    < 4 / unknown
  '7.1'            7.1      5.1       3.1       stereo
  '5.1'            5.1      5.1       3.1       stereo
  '3.1'            3.1      3.1       3.1       stereo

A request never UPGRADES (a '5.1' request on an 8ch sink stays '5.1'); the ladder only steps DOWN to fit. When even 3.1 does not fit (M < 4) the bus fails closed to a WORKING plain-stereo bus (lanes=0, vbap=null) that plays normally; effectiveLayoutOf(name) reports 'stereo'. effectiveLayoutOf(name) returns the BUILT ladder token ('7.1'/'5.1'/'3.1'/'stereo'/null) -- distinct from layoutOf() (sink capability vs per-bus built layout): a '7.1' request on a 6ch sink returns '5.1' here while layoutOf() is '5.1' too, but a '3.1' request on that sink returns '3.1'.

Rings (shared SMPTE lane indices; LFE always index 3, azimuth-invariant distance-only send, never a VBAP gain; y not panned): 7.1 ring [C,R,SR,SBR,SBL,SL,L] az [0,30,110,150,210,250,330,360]; 5.1 drops SBR/SBL -> [C,R,SR,SL,L] az [0,30,110,250,330,360]; 3.1 front-only -> [C,R,L] az [0,30,330,360]. 3.1 has no rear speaker: a source directly behind folds across the 300-degree back gap between R (30) and L (330) -- correct for a front-only rig, a documented limitation. The solver (_vbapSolve) walks a per-preset frozen ring record captured cold on busRec.vbap, so _flushLanes writes EXACTLY busRec.lanes gains (8/6/4) with NO per-tick preset branch, reusing the one Float32Array(8) scratch. destination.channelCount is set to the MAX lane count across live discrete buses (monotonic; buses are add-only), saved-once/restored-verbatim.

Design records: decisions/0003-ducking, 0004-snapshots, 0005-auto-suspend, 0006-dynamic-bus, 0008-detected-layout, 0009-preset-ladder.

### Compat: lite-audio-manager drop-in (v2.0.0)

Import path: `@zakkster/lite-audio/compat`. Exports `AudioManager` (class) and `audioManager` (singleton), extends EventTarget. A game on the unscoped `lite-audio-manager` (Howler overlay) migrates by changing one import; the shim is a pure adapter over lite-audio, no Howler.

- Surface: init / play / playExclusive / playUnique / stop / stopCategory / stopCategories / setMuted / destroy, `isMuted` / `isUnlocked`, the `'mutechange'` CustomEvent, and the same `lite_audio_muted` storage key (mute preference migrates in both directions). An `engine` getter exposes the underlying LiteAudio.
- Classification: a config sound with `loop` or `html5` maps to a streamed lite-audio track (real fades); everything else to a pooled SFX voice. Categories become buses (one per distinct category, auto-created); a stopCategory for a category no sound declared is a silent no-op.
- Divergences (documented, tested): pre-unlock play() returns null but is KEPT and flushed on unlock (DIV-1); stop fade is honored for tracks, inert for pooled SFX (DIV-2); active ids pruned by an isPlaying sweep, not an end event (DIV-3); one Howl type becomes two engine types (DIV-4).
- init() is a synchronous facade over async decode; await whenReady() to assert on a loaded sound. See PARITY.md and decisions/0007-compat-shim.md.

### Reactive readables
`ctxState() : ReadSignal<'suspended'|'running'|'interrupted'|'closed'>`
`unlocked() : ReadSignal<boolean>`
`muted() : ReadSignal<boolean>`
`loadState(id) : ReadSignal<LoadState> | undefined`
`trackLoadState(name), trackPlaying(name), trackPosition(name), trackDuration(name) : ReadSignal | undefined`
`busVolume(name), busMuted(name) : ReadSignal | undefined`
`busNode(name) : GainNode | undefined`
`masterNode() : GainNode | null`

### destroy(): void
Stops every voice, tears down SFX pools, tears down every track (pauses element, disconnects source + gains, removes timeupdate/ended listeners, cancels pending pause timers), disposes every lite-signal node it created (effects AND signals -- per-bus volume/mute, metered level, instance mute/unlock/context-state, per-sound and per-track readouts), releases the per-bus positional scratch, aborts unlock/lifecycle controllers, releases references. Idempotent, so a host that churns engines (route changes, tests, hot reload) returns all pool nodes and never exhausts the shared lite-signal pool. Does not close the AudioContext.

## Handle contract

A `play()` / `playOpts()` / `playUnique()` result is ONE number carrying four kinds of value. Typed as `VoiceHandle | Skipped | TrackStarted` in Audio.d.ts (`VoiceHandle` is a branded number so a raw integer or a track name cannot be passed where a handle belongs).

| Value                       | Meaning                                   | Inert to stop()? |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `0`                         | a REAL handle: bus 0, channel 0, gen 0    | no -- it stops    |
| `busIndex * 2^32 + pool`    | every other real handle                   | no -- it stops    |
| `-1` (Skipped)              | nothing played (unknown/not-ready sound, locked context queued the play, or playUnique throttled) | yes |
| `-2` (TrackStarted)         | playUnique() started a music TRACK (singleton, name-addressed, no handle) | yes |

- **0 cannot be a null sentinel.** It is a perfectly good handle, so "nothing happened" is signalled by NEGATIVES only. Negatives are inert to `stop()` by construction (`if (handle < 0) return`), so a `play()`/`playUnique()` result is safe to pass straight to `stop()` unchecked.
- **Two bit layouts.** The pool handle is `[gen:24][channel:8]` (a uint32, `((gen << 8) | channel) >>> 0`). The engine tags the bus ABOVE those 32 bits: `handle = busIndex * 2^32 + poolHandle`. Decode: `busIndex = (h / 2^32) | 0`, `poolHandle = h >>> 0`. This is why raw pool handles collide across buses (every pool starts at gen 0 / channel 0) and the bus tag is what names one voice.
- **Bus ceiling: 2^21.** The low half is a full uint32, so a handle is an exact integer only while `busIndex <= 2^21 - 1`; bus index 2^21 itself already overflows 2^53. `init()` throws a `RangeError` above 2^21 user buses rather than issue colliding handles. `'master'` is implicit and does not count.
- **SMI note.** A handle leaves V8's SMI range (31-bit signed) on any bus >= 1, and on bus 0 once a channel's generation passes 8,388,608 (~hours of continuous stealing on one channel). It stays a plain number exact to 2^53; the boxed-double cost is below the zero-GC gate's resolution -- measured, see `decisions/0001-handle-namespace.md` and `test/torture.mjs`. Generation WRAPS at 2^24 rather than retiring the channel (voices are scarce and fixed); the divergence from lite-arena's fail-closed retirement is deliberate -- see `decisions/0002-generation-wrap.md`.

## Zero-GC gate

`node --expose-gc test/torture.mjs` -- measures the handle return on bus >= 1 and past generation 8,388,608 (the cases where it leaves SMI range), reports bytesPerOp per regime, and is falsifiable: `LITEAUDIO_TORTURE_LEAK=1 node --expose-gc test/torture.mjs` routes the gated path through the rejected `{bus,handle}`-object design and the gate exits non-zero. The gate also runs the AU1 monitor-tick tier and the S3 spatial tiers -- T-SP1 (setPosition is a zero-alloc scratch stamp), T-SP2 (the ~10 Hz flush holds the native param-event rate under a 200/param/voice cap), and T-SP3 (a lite-leak retention witness proving destroy() releases the per-bus positional scratch across 200 build/teardown cycles), plus the S4 HRTF tier T-SP5 (every voice panner across capacity reports panningModel==='HRTF'; the gain=0 HRIR prewarm retires on the monitor tick with activeCount()===0 and a zero live-node census delta; a lite-leak witness proves destroy() releases the hrtf bus across 200 build/teardown cycles) and the S5 stereo-width tier T-SP6 (the ~10 Hz width flush holds the wet/makeup native-event rate under a 200/param cap with identical-value writes collapsing to exactly 1; setWidth is a zero-alloc stamp at <= 4 B/op with no major GC; a lite-leak witness proves destroy() disconnects + nulls all 7 widener nodes across 200 build/teardown cycles). Each ships a proven red control: LITEAUDIO_TORTURE_SP1_RED / SP2_RED / SP3_RED / SP5_RED / SP6_RED (a 60 Hz per-frame direct param writer that blows the event cap) / SP6_ALLOC_RED (a setWidth that boxes into a retained object) each force the failure that tier guards against, and the gate exits non-zero. `npm run verify` runs the node:test suite and this gate together.

See Audio.js source for full inline documentation.
